_comment: Hand corrections to the reader's output for A10, in pixels of the
full-resolution crops in .build/a10/ (see imageSize / sheetImageSize).
THE BOARD. The reader found 51 of the 92 designators, 55% -- or 65% of the
78 that have a silkscreen designator at all, since the twelve H and MP parts
are rivets, screws, spacers, ejectors, a rubber foot and the heat shield and
are not lettered anywhere. Every one of the 51 was rendered and looked at,
and seven were wrong:
agreed     27 of 29 right   (K4 landed on K1's label, U1 on the '5' of L5)
ambiguous   3 of 4 right    (C1 on the 'AI' of OHMS MAIN ASSEMBLY)
single     13 of 16 right   (K7 on C3, U7 on U1's label, Z1 on 'MAIN')
collision   1 of 2 right    (K1 on K19's label; K19 itself was right)
which is the usual shape: agreed is the best tier and still not a clean one.
All seven are legible on the drawing, so they are replaced by hand below
rather than dropped, along with the 29 the reader never found.
Two clusters caused most of the trouble. The 'OHMS MAIN ASSEMBLY' legend runs
vertically up the right-hand edge of the board and its letters read as C1 and
Z1; and K1/K4/K19 sit in a column of identical relay outlines where a marker
one row out looks entirely plausible.
All five test points are placed by hand as a matter of course. Each is drawn
as a short bar with its label below it, so each box spans bar and label
together -- a marker on the label alone sends a probe about 60 px high of the
pad. TP3's bar sits 23 px left of its label's centre while TP5's is dead
centre, so the boxes are not a constant offset from the lettering.
THE SHEETS. Sheet 1 is the resistance strings and sheet 2 the digital
section; sheets 3 and 4 carry no circuit at all (they are the relay state
tables) and get no reader pass and no placements. Every marker on sheets 1
and 2 was reviewed:
sh1   77 read   51 kept   26 rejected   +  9 placed by hand   = 60
sh2   78 read   47 kept   31 rejected   + 13 placed by hand   = 60
The relay coil rows on sheet 2 and the relay contact groups on sheet 1 read
almost perfectly -- 38 of 38 K markers right on sheet 1, 35 of 35 on sheet 2.
Everything else did badly, and in the ways the pipeline has met before: pin
numbers read as capacitors ('16' as C10, '8' as C4, '13' as C6), package
names as capacitors ('2FCL' as C11, '4FCL' as C7), net names as networks
('INT SENSE HI' as Z2, 'RLH' as R1, '+5RLH' as VR1), and the words of U9's
own output list as the ICs they name ('U6 STB' as U6, 'U12 STB' as U12).
Two blocks are dropped wholesale. Sheet 2's relay bottom-view legend prints
K39.' as plain text beside the package drawings, and the reader placed K9,
K10, K31 and K32 on those words -- in the agreed tier, looking trustworthy.
All four are replaced with their real coil positions. Sheet 1's test point
legend at zone C1 caught TP1, TP2, TP4 and TP5 the same way; those are
replaced with the flag positions on the nets.
Every H and MP designator the reader found on a sheet is a misread by
construction -- rivets, screws and heat shields have no schematic symbol.

_notOnDrawingComment: Twelve mechanical parts with no silkscreen designator. MP1 and MP2, the
swaged brass spacers, are the only ones drawn at all -- two rings near the
left edge -- and nothing on the drawing says which ring is which, so neither
is placed. The rest (rivets, screws, ejectors, the rubber foot and the heat
shield) have no outline either. They stay searchable in the parts list.
_dropSchematicComment: Reads reviewed by eye and rejected. Grouped by what the reader actually saw.
Anything replaced by a hand placement below is not listed here -- a hand
placement already supersedes the read for that sheet.
_schematicComment: Hand placements on the sheets. The five test points are placed on their flag
symbols on sheet 1, checked against the signal name printed beside each one:
TP1 on S COM at P302 32A/32C, TP2 on OHMS SENSE LO at P301 25A/25C, TP3 on
OHMS OUT LO at 24A/24C, TP4 on INT OUT HI at 30A/30C and TP5 on INT SENSE HI
at 28A/28C -- all five agreeing with the legend box at zone C1. No test point
appears on sheet 2 at all: its only commons are LH COM and RLH COM.
K9, K10, K31 and K32 on sheet 2 are their coils in the latching-relay rows,
replacing the legend text the reader read instead. C10, C11 and C12 are the
5801 decoupling capacitors, each printed just below and right of its driver's
designator at the same offset C16 has from U3.

_sheetsComment: The zone grid for each sheet, measured as the inner border of the frame in
pixels of that sheet's own crop and normalised. The crops are cut to the
OUTER border, so the inner frame sits about 60 px inside on every side and
the zone-label band lies between the two. On sheets 1 and 3 the frame's left
border is off the page in the scan, so the crop starts at x=0 and the left
band is already lost; the numbers below are still the inner frame.
_layersComment: Photo alignment. src is board/drawing space, dst is photo image space, and
the homography solved from these maps board -> photo.
The photograph is in the same orientation as the locator drawing and at
nearly the same scale, but it is about 6% shorter vertically relative to it,
so a translation alone will not do -- the offset at the top of the board is
130 px and in the middle it is 15.
Every landmark is a silkscreen OUTLINE corner or a component body, never an
ejector, standoff or mounting hole -- those stand proud of the board and show
real parallax -- and never a designator's lettering, because A10 is one of
the boards where the drawing moves text inside the part outline and the
board does not: K5 is lettered inside its box on the drawing and outside it
